rationale: Y covers far more of the ground-truth concern space: it independently validates the NPU/XPU/MUSA, connector-drain-ordering, full-payload-branch, and prefix-cache items the human reviewer raised, then extends the connector-ownership concern with three concrete counter-examples (other drain call sites) and surfaces a new, well-reasoned image-path bug (GitHub vs MkDocs relative resolution) plus a TP>1 collective caveat—all with precise file:line grounding. X is well-evidenced but narrower, only clearly overlapping on the mkdocs/qwen-asr dependency-conflict item and tangentially on platform scope via a CUDA-only Event citation, missing the connector live-state, full-payload-branch, and prefix-cache threads entirely. Both are grounded and actionable with concrete citations, but Y's broader and deeper coverage gives it a clear recall edge without sacrificing precision.
